summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -7 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +5.3%; weakest: Sugar #11 -16.3%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.04% (-8 bp in a month), 2-year 4.76% (-3 bp); 2s10s curve +28 bp (-5 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.84 (+2.0% in a month, +5.7% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.937 (+18.2% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.668 (-0.1%); USD/MXN 19.05 (+3.4%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -7.0% in a month (+4.8% YTD); VIX 29.6. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 82.40 $/bbl (-15.2% in a month), Brent 89.13, ULSD 3.979 $/gal (-13.1%), natural gas 3.17 (-0.2%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -15.4% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.8%, Hang Seng -5.2%, yuan +0.1% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 9 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (27%); S&P GSCI -11.5% in a month; gold -13.5%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
